_note: footage_plate names the synthetic footage the render check draws the reference on (light_wall or dark_room), chosen to match footage_fit. Five creator intros, torn down as data (KRI-1609 / KRI-1610). Not a template list: a reference is evidence of taste, and each scene is the closest IntroScene today's engine can compile. The example titles are fixtures for the render check (make verify-intro-scenes) and are never used as on-screen text at runtime. Scenes are option ids and one voice per title word, nothing else. Source of the look: the approved taste board https://claude.ai/artifact/QjPSuSE4RGWZDq681BXqiT (2026-11-24).

engine_limits.piece: an entrance time per line (ref 5's serif lands 0.2 s after its script)
engine_limits.move: only accent lines can wait, by the one issued delay (stagger accent_after, 0.6 s); a solid line never waits and no other delay is issued

engine_limits.piece: lines overlapping other than a script tucked onto the serif under it
engine_limits.move: stack script_over_serif is the only overlap: script_serif only, script above serif, at the taste board's B2 geometry; every other pair of lines keeps its gap

engine_limits.piece: flash cover (about 0.1 s) and moment sounds timed to each element
engine_limits.move: a cover/flash element; sounds land only on line entrances (sound_cue accent or each, one library sound id for the whole intro), never on another element

engine_limits.piece: pen-stroke reveal in a face other than Patrick Hand
engine_limits.move: the handwriting effect draws Patrick Hand centerlines whatever font the row names, so the pen entrance is issued only with a Patrick Hand accent; Zeyada and Over the Rainbow reveal with the ink wipe instead

engine_limits.piece: an ink picked from the footage
engine_limits.move: the menu offers every ink; contrast against the footage is left to the existing legibility outline until the engine ranks inks per footage
